source.title: Investigating Alternatives to the Root Mean Square for Adaptive Gradient Methods

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendix
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares adaptive-gradient normalization choices on training loss and task performance, but reports no result on the claim’s training-versus-test generalization gap or its listed measures.
record.gate_note: The reported optimizer comparisons are results on training loss or task scores, not held-out error or training–test gap. The paper discusses the tested tasks and method comparisons; it does not report claim-specific findings. Figure-only curves do not identify held-out metrics.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers on optimization loss and reinforcement-learning scores. Image-classification curves explicitly show training loss; language-modeling curves provide no identified held-out outcome. There is no empirical SGD comparator, so these comparisons do not test V4. No other version receives a direct test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: L3 or L6 normalization improves learning speed and final measured performance, with L6 preferred for their stationary tasks and L3 for reinforcement learning. These are optimization and task-score conclusions, not demonstrated held-out generalization gains. Their comparisons with other adaptive methods are qualified: L6 is competitive on CIFAR-10, rather than uniformly superior.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Lp variants of Adam and other adaptive optimizers; reports training-loss curves and task scores rather than training-versus-test generalization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported optimizer performance varies with the Lp norm, learning rate, task, and task stationarity; L6 performs best in the supervised and unsupervised tasks tested, while L3 performs better in deep reinforcement learning.

fits_no_version.finding: L6 Adam improves image-classification training loss and reported language-modeling loss relative to standard Adam; comparisons with other adaptive methods vary by task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing Adam's gradient-normalization exponent can improve optimization performance after learning-rate selection.

fits_no_version.finding: L3 Adam improves DQN scores over standard Adam in three Atari games and achieves comparable scores in three others.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam's normalization exponent can affect reinforcement-learning task performance.

record.problems: The figures show standard-deviation shading over 3 trials (10 for MNIST), but no claim-specific generalization-gap measurement is reported. Several numerical outcomes are shown only as plotted curves.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported measurements are optimizer training loss and reinforcement-learning scores, not outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected held-out comparisons and effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, including the specified remedies.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation should change from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. Its empty rows and labels are justified. Missing generalization-gap measurements alone would not exclude V4, which requires held-out performance rather than necessarily a measured gap; here neither an identified held-out comparison nor an empirical SGD baseline is supplied. The omitted optimization results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
